content.jointProblem: Can a probabilistic and sequence model trained on Subotička Mobilnost's 10-second AVL archive produce PassengerView stop-level ETAs that stay within 90 seconds of actual arrival at least 85% of the time, including peak, roadworks and weather disruption? The first experiment would test transfer of Novaković's state-space and GRU methods to the company's 340-bus, 2.8-billion-row PostgreSQL AVL stream and establish a joint evaluation protocol before any deployment.

rationale.text: Novaković's doctoral work is directly on Bayesian state-space models for bus travel time estimation from archived AVL data.

sources.quote: dissertation on Bayesian state-space models for bus travel time estimation using archived AVL data

rationale.text: She has published segment-level travel time estimation from AVL records, reporting an 18% MAE reduction over a historic-average baseline.

sources.quote: Segment-level mean absolute error (MAE) is reduced by 18% compared with a historic-average baseline.

rationale.text: She has evaluated LSTM and GRU architectures for stop-level arrival prediction from historical AVL sequences.

sources.quote: GRU achieves mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 8.3%

rationale.text: Her group has tested transfer from Novi Sad AVL data to the Subotica bus network, reporting 52 seconds MAE per stop-to-stop segment after fine-tuning.

sources.quote: fine-tuned model achieves MAE of 52 seconds per stop-to-stop segment

rationale.text: She has built a systematic AVL preprocessing pipeline and released it as open-source Python modules.

sources.quote: Code is provided as open-source Python modules.

rationale.text: She has benchmarked probabilistic travel time models under extreme weather, including conformal prediction for coverage.

sources.quote: Conformal prediction maintains nominal 90% coverage most consistently, at the cost of wider intervals.

rationale.text: Her project REALBUS targets lightweight models that can be retrained nightly on a standard server without GPU hardware.

sources.quote: retrained nightly on a standard server

rationale.text: She has prior industry experience auditing a municipal operator's AVL archive under a service contract.

sources.quote: collaborated under a service contract with the Novi Sad city public transport operator to audit their AVL data archive

constraints.text: The PassengerView contracts require displayed ETAs to be within 90 seconds of actual arrival at least 85% of the time; the evaluation protocol must define actual arrival and test peak, roadworks and weather conditions.

sources.quote: displayed ETAs to be within 90 seconds of the bus's actual arrival at least 85 percent of the time

constraints.text: The work depends on access to the company's full historical AVL dataset and timetable logs under a signed data-sharing agreement, with fields including timestamp, vehicle ID, line ID, stop sequence, door-open events and odometer.

sources.quote: access to our full historical AVL dataset and timetable logs under a signed data-sharing agreement
The AVL data includes timestamp, vehicle ID, line ID, stop sequence, door-open events and odometer.

constraints.text: The model must fit the existing PassengerView and GTFS-Realtime integration path, the Java/Spring and Python preprocessing stack, the on-premise Kubernetes cluster, and the 12-month contract window.

sources.quote: Java 17 backend with Spring Boot microservices
Docker and Kubernetes on on-premise cluster in Subotica data centre
twelve-month implementation window starting from go-live approval

constraints.text: Weather data is not integrated, so any weather-dependent model needs a data source or a weather-blind variant tested first.

sources.quote: We do not have weather data integrated yet.

constraints.text: The company can dedicate only one senior backend engineer and one domain specialist part-time, and its current data engineer has no time-series modelling background; knowledge transfer and maintenance must be planned.

sources.quote: one senior backend engineer and one domain specialist part-time
We have one data engineer on staff who knows Python well but has no background in time-series modelling.

constraints.text: Novaković's stated workload is moderate and she can take on one new collaboration in 2026, so start date and effort must be confirmed.

sources.quote: Workload is moderate; she can take on one new collaboration in 2026.

risks: Published accuracy is not the contract metric: her 41-second RMSE is for 15-minute-ahead predictions and her 52-second MAE is per stop-to-stop segment, while the contract requires end-to-end arrival ETAs within 90 seconds at least 85% of the time. The first experiment must replicate the SLA on company data.

Transfer gap: methods were developed and tested on Novi Sad archives or on Subotica data with limited fine-tuning; the company's 340-bus 10-second data may differ in network topology and operations, and gains beyond about 8 weeks of fine-tuning data were limited in her transfer study.
Sampling mismatch: her low-frequency AVL filter assumes 30–90-second pings, while the company collects 10-second pings; preprocessing and model assumptions need revalidation on the denser stream.

Missing covariates: her extreme-weather models rely on weather data that the company has not integrated, and APC passenger-load models rely on counters not listed in the company AVL fields; load-aware gains may not transfer without those inputs.

Staffing and maintenance: the company has one Python data engineer without time-series modelling background, so a research-grade model could be hard to retrain, monitor and maintain after the project.

Availability, publication and format are not fully settled: participation marks availability and industrial PhD supervision as unknown, while her notes give one new collaboration in 2026 and a preference for the right to publish anonymised results.
Regulatory and multi-jurisdiction deployment: the Romanian contracts involve three authorities and require data segregation and regulatory documentation for multi-jurisdiction operators.

Timeline: the 12-month implementation window starting from Q3 2024 and the planned mid-2025 GTFS-Realtime PassengerView release may be tight for research, validation and deployment; no budget is stated.
questions: What exactly counts as the bus's actual arrival for the 90-second/85% SLA—door-open event, stop-line crossing, or another signal—and which lines, periods and disruption conditions are in scope for acceptance?
Will the full historical AVL archive and timetable logs be available under the signed data-sharing agreement, and what known data-quality issues exist in the 2.8-billion-row PostgreSQL table?
Can weather data be integrated for this project, or should the first model be weather-blind and tested without weather covariates?
Are APC passenger counts available for any vehicles, or only door-open events and odometer? If counters are not available, can door-open events serve as a dwell-time proxy?
How will a Python model be served inside the Java/Spring, on-premise Kubernetes PassengerView stack, and who will own retraining, monitoring and GTFS-Realtime output after the project?
Does Novaković have capacity starting in 2026, and can the company accept her group's preference to publish anonymised results?
Participation leaves industrial PhD supervision willingness unknown; is the company interested in that format, or should this remain a joint project?
What budget and compute are available for model development, data engineering and ongoing maintenance?
Is the Q3 2024 go-live assumption and the 12-month Romanian contract window still the operative timeline?
